question: Why does guessing 2, 4, 7 crack the rule faster than 3, 6, 12?
answer: The hidden rule is just "numbers in ascending order". Every doubling triple also rises, so its yes can't tell ×2 apart from the real rule. 2, 4, 7 is the test where ×2 says no, and the rule still says yes, so the guess breaks.
move: Test what could prove you wrong, not what agrees with you.

web.label: Tap-to-test card on confirmation bias. Four number triples (3, 6, 12; 10, 20, 40; 2, 4, 7; 100, 200, 400) can be tapped to test a hidden rule. Asks why guessing 2, 4, 7 cracks the rule faster than the doubling triples.
